statement: For any actual closed locally compact free proper two-dimensional interior disk action Q, every based positive-dimensional sphere family in its boundary-fixed centralizer contracts in that same topological group. The proof uses the actual simply transitive Lie action and the compact three-word estimate to retain the specified disk boundary, without a closed-disk conjugacy assumption. An explicit proper cyclic rectangular compactification has no closed-disk Fuchsian conjugacy and makes the corresponding partial-boundary restriction map nonsurjective; its full boundary-fixed centralizer is nevertheless explicitly topologically identified with a group of periodic real-fiber families and is contractible.
depends_on: C.33 actual proper Lie action and principal orbit comparison; C.37.2 exact three-word fractional-power estimate; the displayed compact restriction embedding, rectangular compactification, actual boundary fixed-set comparison, periodic-fiber group isomorphism and topology proof
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), admissible infinite-operator level-zero comparison and relative disk centralizers.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The original disk, actual interior restricted closure, the full boundary-relative topology, every coordinate map and inverse, and the obstruction to the proposed closed-disk conjugacy are retained.
computational_checks: code/part_b/c71_disk_compactification_certificate.py and its adjacent JSON/stdout pass 34,194 exact rational and symbolic checks of the compactification maps, translation formulas, actual boundary and partial-quotient comparisons, and nonlinear periodic fiber examples with exact interpolation/inverse identities.
notes: The two-dimensional conclusion concerns every based sphere family, not an asserted global contraction of the entire relative group. The cyclic model does have a full explicit contraction. Its actual relative centralizer orbits are vertical lines, so the model does not provide an open transitive orbit. The general zero- and one-dimensional proper-operator boundary comparison, nonfixed-frontier extension and general C.12 remain unresolved.
